text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Israeli President Weizman, Jordan's King Hussein discuss Syria peace track.
- Government says tourism down 15 percent from last year.
- Elbit returns to the black; Teledata reports record revenue.
- Bankers say: Lauder's bid for Africa-Israel bound to fail.
- Carmel bank seeks to buy Maritime Bank.
- Foreign Ministry distributes list of alleged Palestinian infractions of interim peace deals that its legal department recommended against since not all allegations would hold up.
- Institute named after former prime minister Shimon Peres takes on former army and Shin Bet secret police officers for information campaign on peace deals with Palestinians.
- Plan to sell controlling stakes in banks presented.
- U.S. is calming: Pressure on Israel not expected now.
- In Israel it's thought Clinton will now get personally involved in negotiations with Palestinians.
- Finance Minister Meridor rejects request of potential buyers to acquire Mercantile Discount without a tender.
